Workflow

Running a club

The club lens replaces Breeze: roster with dual status, groups, follow-ups, events, dues and the officer year. The Federation sees counts, never names.

Built in the Hub
Partly built Roster, officers, households, dues and remittance, groups, follow-ups and club events are built (B1, B2). The secretary's queue, condolence surface, club migration, club giving (B3) and the Breeze import (B4) are not built.
Branches
All branches
Shared services
Membership and standing, Events, Funds and ledger, Directory and communications
Governed by
D1 · D6 · R6 · R16 · S7

Steps

  1. Read the roster with national and club status side by side, sorted by householdClub officer
  2. Make groups and raise follow-ups with due datesClub secretary or officer
  3. Run the treasurer's month: collect, close, remit, reconcileClub treasurer
  4. File officers and the affiliation by the By-Law 3.2 deadlineClub president or secretary
  5. Select the delegation for conventionClub officers
  6. Hand over grants at the end of the officer yearOutgoing and incoming officers
  7. See a club's groups, events and follow-ups as counts under the floorFederation staff

Hands off to

  • club → ledger: collections are attested and remitted on the run (D1)
  • club → comms: a club mailing reaches only its own roster, consent-filtered
  • club → convention: the delegation is selected and credentialed against standing
  • club → reporting: the Federation roll-up shows counts, never names

Programmes that use it

All, through the shared services.

Open

  • Which club goes first for the Breeze import, and who holds its key (Breeze Parity §5 q4).
  • Whether the club register holds 17, 18 or 19 clubs (§5 q8).
  • The affiliation form's content is not held.
